## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag does not take a default from the `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, which the project's CLI flag reference requires for every new flag under `cli/`. Exclusions that CI sets through the environment are therefore ignored.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option. `collect` uses `fnmatch` to skip files whose basename matches any of the patterns and logs each skipped file. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds tests at the parser, `collect` and `main` levels.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — If CI runs with `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` and passes no `--exclude`, `.log` files still go into the archive, because the default is the hard-coded `default=[]`. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable … because CI sets options through the environment." — CI jobs that configure exclusions through the environment will build archives containing files they meant to leave out, and nothing warns them. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose and document a separator for multiple patterns in `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the variable being set.
